title: Operational authorization flow and checkpointed model promotion
creator: Anika Desai
description:
Problem: Teams need a predictable, minimally disruptive way to promote model variants through canary -> A/B -> full production paths while ensuring auditable approvals, least-privilege signoff, and deterministic auto-rollback when metrics regress. Current ad-hoc approvals (Slack threads + PR comments) lack structured evidence, expire unpredictably, and make postmortems slow.

Scope: Deliver a product-managed authorization flow for model promotions that covers: checkpoint gates for each promotion stage, RBAC-driven signoff windows, cryptographically-anchored audit snapshots, required role combinations per promotion tier, lightweight UI & API for request + signoff, and automatic rollback triggers wired to evaluation SLOs. Integrations: Console (signoff UI), API (promotion requests), Audit logs (immutable snapshot storage), Routing (canary/ab/shadow traffic controls), and Alerts (Grafana/SLO triggers).

Non-goals: Implementing novel model evaluation metrics or redesigning serving kernels. This work assumes existing metric ingestion and canary routing primitives from ENG.

High-level approach:
1) Define promotion tiers and required signoffs: "light promotion" (owner + SRE), "sensitive promotion" (owner + Security + SRE), "entitled promotion" (owner + Product + Security + SRE). Each approval must be explicit and timeboxed (default expiry 72h).
2) RBAC artifacts: map product teams, model owners, platformops, security, and SRE to approval roles; provide ephemeral approval tokens that can be revoked.
3) Evidence snapshot: when a promotion request is created, capture a read-only bundle (model hash, config diff, canary config, metric snapshot, PR/Confluence links) and store it in immutable audit logs with a tamper-evident signature.
4) UI/UX: lightweight console flow to create requests, display evidence bundle, and collect signoffs; allow multi-signature progression with configurable quorum rules.
5) Auto-rollback: define declarative rollback conditions tied to canary SLOs (latency/error/quality thresholds) plus a cooldown and rollback audit entry.
6) Emergency overrides: emergency rollback operator role with required two-person approval and mandatory incident ticket link.

Success criteria: clear, repeatable promotion flow in Console + API; ability to query audit history by model version; automatic rollback executes within SLO windows when triggers fire; reduced manual approvals via delegated short-lived approvals for low-risk promotions.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Create promotion request UI that attaches snapshot and displays required signoff matrix
RBAC: Approval roles mapped and configurable via Console (PlatformOps, ModelOwner, SRE, Security, Product)
Timeboxed approvals: Delegated approvals expire by default after 72 hours and are shown as expired in UI
Audit: Promotion snapshot saved immutably and queryable (model-hash, config-diff, metrics, links)
API: Promotion request + signoff endpoints implemented and covered by integration tests
Auto-rollback: Canary rollback triggers correctly evaluate SLO breaches and execute rollback path; rollback event logged
Emergency override: Two-person emergency rollback flow exists with incident link requirement
Metrics: Pilot with 3 internal model teams shows >50% reduction in round-trip approval time for low-risk promotions
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial scoping sync — aligned on three promotion tiers. Decision: default expiry 72h for delegated approvals (suggested by Security). Action: ENG to provide API hooks for snapshot capture (ENG-4123).

2026-02-22: SRE feedback — require SRE signoff for any promotion that increases concurrency or alters KV caching behavior. Added as rule in acceptance criteria. ENG assigned to add concurrency flag to promotion request payload (ENG-4312).

2026-02-25: Security review kickoff — Security requests cryptographic anchoring of snapshots and an audit export API for compliance. Security emphasized revocation semantics for delegated tokens. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-02-27: Prototype PR opened for API endpoints and DB schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4928 — includes promotion_requests table and audit_blob storage. Requesting initial review from Platform Eng.

2026-02-28: Internal pilot plan agreed: three internal teams (Search, Summarization, Assistants) will use flow in staged pilot; runbook for pilot created and linked below. Pilot will run for two weeks followed by a retro.
2026-03-01: UX updated per feedback — added visible expiry timestamp, delegation history, and 'why required' tooltips for each signoff role. Preparing for ENG integration testing next sprint.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: lightweight approval UX vs. thorough evidence capture — decided to present summary first and require full bundle only for sensitive tiers.
Open questions: policy for delegated approval lineage (how many hops, who can re-delegate) — follow-up with Legal and Security in next week.
Follow-ups: ENG to implement immutability guarantees for audit_blob and provide HMAC-signed proofs; Security to validate signing key rotation plan.
